newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - David Jones warns on year profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - David Jones warns on year profit.

text.p: Upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Tuesday its current year profit is likely to be lower than last year if sales did not improve materially.

"If sales do not materially improve through the rest of the financial year, then it is likely that the profit before tax will be below last year," said David Jones chairman Dick Warburton told the annual general meeting.
Warburton said the retail market had remained tough since the end of the financial year at end-July.
"As of yet, we have seen few signs of any uplift in consumer confidence," he said.
David Jones' sales for the first quarter and the resulting operating profit were below the same period last year.

"The widespread industry nature of Australia's depressed consumer confidence is evident from the frequent reports of companies reassessing their profit and dividend forecasts -- whether they be aligned to the building industry, retailing, manufacturing or whatever," he said.
Warburton said David Jones was seeing increased competition for the consumer dollar from a variety of sources including leisure, entertainment, recreation and tourism.

"Concurrent with those cyclical and structural changes, we have seen a considerable amount of discounting by all the other retailers in the department store sector, providing further proof that the depressed consumer spending is industry based and not confined to David Jones," Warburton said.
He said it was difficult to predict when the cyclical improvement would occur, but that the company was confident it had strategies in place to take full advantage of any upturn.
David Jones in November reported that its sales in the 1996/97 first quarter fell 2.9 percent from a year earlier to A$310.5 million.
David Jones reported sales of A$1.44 billion in the year to July 27, 1996 and a net profit of A$67.53 million.
